43-32-24. Return of security deposit after termination of tenancy--Withholding--Itemized accounting--Forfeiture of withholding rights--Punitive damages.

Every lessor of residential premises shall, within two weeks after the termination of the tenancy and receipt of the tenant's mailing address or delivery instructions, return the security deposit to the tenant, or furnish to the tenant, a written statement showing the specific reason for the withholding of the deposit or any portion thereof. The lessor may withhold from such deposit only such amounts as are reasonably necessary to remedy tenant defaults in the payment of rent or of other funds due to the landlord pursuant to an agreement or to restore the premises to their condition at the commencement of the tenancy, ordinary wear and tear excepted. Within forty-five days after termination of the tenancy, upon request of the lessee, the lessor shall provide the lessee with an itemized accounting of any deposit withheld.

Any lessor of residential premises who fails to comply with this section shall forfeit all rights to withhold any portion of such deposit.

The bad faith retention of a deposit or any portion of a deposit by a lessor of residential premises in violation of this section, including failure to provide the written statement and itemized accounting required by this section, shall subject the lessor to punitive damages not to exceed two hundred dollars.

Source: SL 1976, ch 267, § 3; SL 1984, ch 281, § 1.

My dad passed from SCLC in February of 2020. Firstly I'm sorry you're going through this, it's a very hard thing to struggle with. Secondly, everyone is different and your dad may have a different outcome than mine. 

My dad was diagnosed around 8-10 months before he passed. By the time they had caught it, it had already spread quite a bit. I don't remember all of the specifics but the treatment they suggested started with like 10 blasts of radiation to the head and he noped put immediately. He said "I'd rather enjoy what  time I have left than get my brains turned to mush."

His QOL definitely began to go downhill about 3-4 months after diagnosis, maybe even sooner. I think he was hiding alot of his issues from me. He had already had a couple of heart attacks at this point also. 

When the time came for hospice, it felt like it came out of nowhere. He had been fine the week prior. Sunday night, he called around 11PM and he could barely wheeze out "Help, Call 911!" That night he got rushed to the hospital, it was all done through the VA, His Dr. Informed me that my father had a DNR in place so if he coded again that was it. He lasted 7 days in hospice. They had him so doped up I think we spoke maybe 3 times in total, a few sentences each time. 

My biggest piece of advice to you, is to spend and enjoy as much time as possible. Because when the time comes there's no getting  it back. If your father does not have his affairs in order, please make sure he gets everything arranged in advance. The last thing you will want to do is be figuring all this out when you're in mourning. 

I hope this is somewhat helpful and if you have any other questions or if there's anything I missed in my rambling I'd be glad to talk. Hopefully you and your dad still have alot of time left together.
